Adults aged 18 or over can pay up to £20,000 into ISAs in the 2026/27 tax year (6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027). You can split this between cash ISAs, stocks and shares ISAs, innovative finance ISAs and a Lifetime ISA. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000. Any unused allowance does not carry forward.

From 6 April 2027, investors under 65 will be capped at £12,000 a year in cash ISAs. The overall £20,000 allowance is unchanged. Details are in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The ISA allowance for 2026/27 is £20,000 per adult aged 18 or over. The tax year runs from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027.

You can split the £20,000 between cash ISAs, stocks and shares ISAs, innovative finance ISAs and a Lifetime ISA. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000. Unused allowance does not carry forward.

[ISAs: a guide for clients › Lifetime ISA]
A Lifetime ISA can be opened by anyone aged 18 to 39. Up to £4,000 a year can be paid in, counting towards the £20,000 overall allowance, and the government adds a 25% bonus of up to £1,000 a year. Money can be withdrawn without charge to buy a first home costing £450,000 or less, provided the account has been open for at least 12 months, from age 60, or if you are terminally ill with less than 12 months to live. Other withdrawals incur a 25% government charge. The government is consulting on a new first-time-buyer ISA to replace the Lifetime ISA; Lifetime ISAs can still be opened until the new product is available, and existing accounts continue under the current rules.

rows.answer:
You can pay up to £4,000 a year into a Lifetime ISA. That counts towards the £20,000 overall allowance. The government adds a 25% bonus of up to £1,000 a year.

Money can be withdrawn without charge in three cases:
- To buy a first home costing £450,000 or less, provided the account has been open for at least 12 months.
- From age 60.
- If you are terminally ill with less than 12 months to live.

Other withdrawals incur a 25% government charge. The source is the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

rows.answer:
A Lifetime ISA can only be opened by people aged 18 to 39, so at 42 you can't open a new one.

The documents don't say whether other ISAs would suit you. Each adult can pay up to £20,000 into ISAs in the 2026/27 tax year. If you want to know what to do with your money, I can pass you to an adviser.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The guide lists these changes from 6 April 2027:

- Investors under 65 can pay no more than £12,000 a tax year into cash ISAs. The overall £20,000 allowance is unchanged, so the rest can go into stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs. Investors aged 65 and over keep a £20,000 cash ISA limit.
- Transfers from stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs into cash ISAs will no longer be permitted.
- A charge will apply to interest paid on cash held inside a stocks and shares or innovative finance ISA.
- Money already in cash ISAs is not affected by the cap.

This is general information, not advice. Your adviser can discuss what it means for you. More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The £12,000 cash ISA cap is for investors under 65, so it wouldn't apply to you at 70. From 6 April 2027, investors aged 65 and over keep a £20,000 cash ISA limit. That is the same as the overall ISA allowance, which is unchanged.

Money already in cash ISAs isn't affected by the cap. From the same date, transfers from stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs into cash ISAs will no longer be permitted.

More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Transfers are started by the receiving provider. Once we receive their request, HMRC guidelines say ISA transfers should complete within 30 calendar days. Transfers between cash ISAs should take no more than 15 working days. Moving holdings as they are (re-registration in specie) can take longer if fund managers are slow to respond.

If your holdings are sold first (a cash transfer), the proceeds move once the sales have settled. That is normally within four working days of dealing. We don't charge for transfers in or out. We keep you informed through the portal at each stage.

Yes. Our stocks and shares ISA is flexible. You can replace money you withdraw during a tax year in that same tax year, and the replacement doesn't use any more of your allowance.

The 2026/27 tax year runs from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027. Unused allowance doesn't carry forward. More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

[Support through life events › Bereavement]
If a client has died, please let us know as soon as you are able; you can also use the Death Notification Service, which tells several financial firms at once. When we are notified, any discretionary mandate ends and the portfolio is held as it is until the personal representatives instruct us. Our management and custody fees stop from the date of death; fund charges continue within the funds until holdings are sold or transferred. We provide a date-of-death valuation for the estate free of charge.

We will need:

- the original or a certified copy of the death certificate;
- details of the executors or administrators of the estate;
- the grant of probate or letters of administration (in Scotland, Confirmation) before assets can be released. Where the total value held with us is below £30,000 we can usually release assets to the personal representatives without a grant, against a signed indemnity.

An ISA continues to be tax-free as a continuing account of a deceased investor for up to three years while the estate is administered. A named member of the team stays with you throughout.
Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/life-events/

rows.answer:
The annual allowance is £60,000. This counts the total paid into your pensions in a tax year, including employer contributions and the value of any defined benefit accrual. If you go over it, an annual allowance charge is normally due.

- **Tapering:** For high earners, the allowance tapers down to a minimum of £10,000.
- **Carry forward:** You can carry forward unused allowance from the previous three tax years. You must have been a member of a registered pension scheme in those years.
- **Money purchase annual allowance:** If you have taken taxable income flexibly from a defined contribution pension, a £10,000 money purchase annual allowance applies to further defined contribution contributions.

More detail is in the pensions guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

I can't advise on what you should do in your own situation. If you'd like that, I can pass you to an adviser.

Yes, you can still pay in, but a lower limit applies. Once you've taken taxable income flexibly from a defined contribution pension, the money purchase annual allowance of £10,000 applies to further defined contribution contributions.

Your own contributions get tax relief up to 100% of your relevant UK earnings in the tax year, or £3,600 gross if your earnings are lower. Basic-rate relief is added to the pension automatically. Higher- and additional-rate taxpayers claim the extra relief through their tax return.

The documents don't say whether paying in is right for you. For that, I can pass you to an adviser.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Up to 25% of a pension can normally be taken tax free, subject to the lump sum allowance of £268,275 across all your pensions. Lump sums above that allowance are taxed at your marginal rate.

I can't advise on how much you should take or what to do with your own money. If you'd like that, I can pass you to an adviser. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

You can draw from a defined contribution pension from age 55. This rises to 57 from 6 April 2028. The options are flexi-access drawdown, buying an annuity, taking lump sums, or a combination. Each has different tax consequences.

When you apply to access a pension, we will refer you to Pension Wise and offer to book a free guidance appointment. We won't do this if you've already had one or have received regulated advice.

I can't tell you which option suits you. If you want advice on that, I can pass you to an adviser.

More detail: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Yes. If the transfer value is more than £30,000, the law requires you to take appropriate independent advice before the transfer can proceed. The advice must come from a firm with Financial Conduct Authority permission to advise on pension transfers. Fernhill Wealth holds that permission.

The Financial Conduct Authority expects advisers to start from the assumption that a transfer won't be suitable. We recommend one only where we can show it is clearly in your interest. The documents don't cover transfers below £30,000.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Based on our pensions guide, the rules are changing:

- **From 6 April 2027:** most unused pension funds and death benefits will count towards the value of your estate for inheritance tax. Benefits passing to a spouse or civil partner, or to a registered charity, stay exempt. Dependants' scheme pensions and death-in-service benefits are outside the new rules.
- **Income tax on death benefits:** if you die before 75, benefits are normally paid free of income tax, within the lump sum and death benefit allowance of £1,073,100. If you die at or after 75, the recipient pays income tax at their marginal rate.

The guide doesn't say how this applies to your own circumstances. Please raise that with your adviser. You can also nominate who receives your pension by completing an expression of wish form. It isn't binding, but the scheme administrator takes it into account.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/
